text:
zara_customer: Hey team — after the Llama4B hotfix swap this morning our webhook consumer started getting broken payloads. Responses that used to be single JSON objects are being split into multiple chunks and sometimes an extra "null" token shows up between fields. example from our logs:

zara_customer: ```
POST /callback 200
Body received (concatenated):
{"order_id":123,"items":[{"sku":"A1","qty":1}],"metadata":null}{"billing":{"total":9.99}}
```

zara_customer: We see two JSON objects stuck together, which breaks our parser. This started right after the model change at ~2171109000. Any clues? :frowning:

anna_support: sorry about that, we're looking. Can you share the request_id or the raw request body + request_ts?

zara_customer: request_id=cli_0x9f7a, request_ts=2171112190. Raw body attached above. Parser errors are `Unexpected token { in JSON at position 1` because our consumer concatenates chunks thinking it's one object.

anna_support: got it, tagging eng. @devon_ml can you take a look?

devon_ml: @anna_support @zara_customer looking. Quick hypothesis: Llama4B hotfix introduced a change in chunk framing that can emit separate JSON documents when the model returns two top-level objects (e.g., metadata followed by billing). Runtime should stream them with clear chunk boundaries, but it seems some clients concatenate without separators. Do you use streaming or non-streaming API?

zara_customer: we're using the normal non-streaming /v1/generate with `response_mode: "structured"`. We noticed the model sometimes puts metadata and result as separate top-level objects in the same response stream.

devon_ml: OK. Two action items: 1) immediate workaround: pin to `model=llama4b@20240715` (previous build) or set `response_mode: "raw"` to avoid structured chunking. 2) longer fix: runtime patch to merge adjacent top-level JSON fragments when they belong to one logical response, and make chunk metadata explicit.

matt_platform: I just created INC-12345 for this as a Sev-2. SRE bot note: incident created and oncall paged. :rotating_light:

srebot: Incident INC-12345 created by matt_platform. Pager issued to eng-oncall. Links: https://incidents.redwood/INC-12345

anna_support: @zara_customer do you want us to roll you back to the previous model on your account while we patch? We can do a model pin on your tenant for the next 24h.

zara_customer: yes please. Pin me back if that's low effort. Also, any chance for billing credit? We had 15 failed webhook processing events that triggered retries and duplicate downstream work.

billing_bot: Ticket BILL-789 created for review. Potential one-time credit being evaluated.

devon_ml: For the engineering side: repro steps I used locally:

devon_ml: ```
# repro: call indoors with structured mode and simulated chunking
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -d '{"model":"llama4b@latest","response_mode":"structured","prompt":"..."}' \
  | jq -R -s 'split("\n")'
```

devon_ml: I also saw `\u0000` markers inserted between fragments in the raw stream. That plus a minor change in the model output leads some SDKs to treat fragments as separate JSON docs. Patch is to normalize and emit a single well-formed JSON object per response unless `stream:true` is used.

anna_support: ETA on canary/patch?

devon_ml: Eng will cut a canary tonight (in ~6h) to the staging pool, then we can push to a small set of tenants. If that looks good we'll roll an emergency production fix in ~12-18h. For immediate relief the tenant pin should prevent more hits.

zara_customer: Pin applied, thanks. I'll monitor and report any new parser failures.

matt_platform: FYI ops: we increased the logging around streaming frames for the next 12h to capture any malformed boundaries. If we see it again, please include raw socket dump.

zara_customer: one more thing — our parser tolerates concatenated objects if they're separated by whitespace/newline, but the inserted nulls are what trip our JSON library. Is there a recommended client-side defensive parsing approach?

devon_ml: short-term: if you must handle this client-side, split on `\u0000` and newlines and parse fragments individually, then merge keys. Eg: `raw.split(/\u0000|\n+/).filter(Boolean).map(JSON.parse)` — then reconcile duplicates (last-wins). It's hacky but workable until runtime fix.

zara_customer: thanks, we'll implement that as a fallback.

anna_support: keeping the thread open. We'll update when canary is live and when billing completes. :white_check_mark:

devon_ml: follow-up: found the root cause — tokenizer boundary change in the hotfix caused the model to emit two adjacent top-level objects when generation completed sooner than the post-processing step expected. Patch will perform a final aggregation pass over fragments before handing them to the structured serializer. Canary target: 2171118000.

matt_platform: canary scheduled. Notified a subset of hosted tenants and our internal QA.

srebot: Canary rollout started at 2171118000 to 8% nodes. Monitoring metrics: parse_errors, chunk_boundary_misses.

anna_support: update for @zara_customer — canary is live. Please let us know if you see failures after 2171118000.

zara_customer: confirmed — no further broken payloads in the last 30m. Thanks for the quick turnaround, team. :clap:

billing_bot: BILL-789: proposed credit 100 USD pending approval.

anna_support: closing note: we kept the tenant pinned until the patch fully rolled out. We'll notify you when the pin is removed (or you can request earlier). Thanks for the clear repro info, it made the triage much faster.

zara_customer: appreciate it, please remove the pin when safe.

matt_platform: incident INC-12345 resolved after canary validation. Root cause: tokenizer boundary change in Llama4B hotfix. Postmortem scheduled for Monday.

srebot: Incident INC-12345 status: resolved. Postmortem scheduled: 2171180000.

anna_support: thread closed but will reopen if any regressions appear. :slightly_smiling_face:
